title: Micro-ROS Robot Control System
summary: A lightweight robot control stack built on micro-ROS for reliable motion commands, telemetry, and embedded edge coordination.
content:
This project focused on building a compact robot control system around micro-ROS so an embedded controller could communicate cleanly with a higher-level ROS 2 stack.

I designed the communication layer to publish wheel odometry, IMU readings, and battery telemetry while subscribing to velocity commands from the navigation pipeline. The control loop ran on a microcontroller with deterministic timing, which kept motion smooth even when wireless traffic spiked.

Core work

Key milestones included tuning PID loops for differential drive motion, defining custom ROS message schemas for diagnostics, and adding watchdog-based safety stops for command loss and motor faults.

The result was a control system that made it easy to move from simulation to hardware while still keeping the embedded layer observable and maintainable.

title: AI Vision Grasping System
summary: An OpenCV and deep-learning grasping pipeline that detects objects, estimates pick points, and guides a robotic arm for repeatable pickup tasks.
content:
This system combined RGB camera input, OpenCV preprocessing, and a lightweight neural detector to identify graspable objects on a tabletop scene.

I built the pipeline to segment the workspace, detect object contours, estimate object orientation, and convert image coordinates into robot arm positions through a calibrated camera-to-arm transform.

Technical focus

The most important improvements came from image normalization, contour filtering, and a grasp ranking strategy that rejected unstable picks near cluttered edges. The arm controller then executed the best candidate grasp with approach, grip, and retreat phases.

In testing, the system significantly improved first-attempt pick success for small consumer objects under mixed lighting.

title: Voice-Controlled Robot Assistant
summary: A voice-command interface for a service robot that maps spoken intents to navigation, object lookup, and simple task execution.
content:
This project explored how to make a mobile robot easier to use by adding a speech-driven command layer on top of its existing navigation and task modules.

I connected speech-to-text with an intent parser that mapped phrases like "go to the charging station" or "bring the toolbox" into structured commands. A dispatcher service validated those intents and triggered the right ROS actions for movement, item lookup, or status reporting.

What mattered

The main engineering work went into handling noisy speech, confirming ambiguous requests, and building fallbacks when the robot could not safely execute a command. I also added spoken feedback so the system felt responsive and transparent to the operator.

The final assistant was simple, but it proved that natural voice interaction could reduce operator friction for routine service tasks.
